To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

transfection of a PD-ECGF cDNA expressing dThd Pase sensitizes tumour cells to 5'-dFUR and tegafu, and that the transfected cells are able to potently enhance the cytotoxicity of 5'-dFU towards co-cultivated parental cells.

transfection of tumours with a human platele-derived endothelial cell-growth factor complementary DNA (c-DNA) encoding thymidine phosphoryylase (dThDPase) sensitizes tumours cells to pyrimidine antimatabolites in vitro and potentiates the cytotoxic effects towards co-cultued parental cells.

transfection of human lung adenocarcine cells (PC-9) with human platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) cDNA expressing dThd Pase sensitizes the cells to the cytotxic effects of pyrimidene antimetobolites, and that the transfected cells are able to poteniate the cytotoxicity of 5'-deoxy-5-flourouridine (5-DFUR) towards co-cultued parental PC-9 cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new therapeutic strategies to treat cancer by using the bystander effect of gene therapy and the selective activation of anticancer prodrugs by tumour-specific gene expression of dThd Pase.
the development of a new strategy for cancer treatment using a gene transfer technique.
the development of a gene therapy strategy using a PD-ECGF cDNA expressing dThd-Pase to sensitize tumour cells to the cytotoxity of pyrimidine antinmetabolites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
transfection of a human PD-ECGF cDNA into tumour cells may be a novel approach for the treatment of tumours resistant to 5-Fu.
the transfection of PDGF-ECGF cDNA into tumour cells can increase the sensitivity of the cells to 5-FUR and its prodrugs.
transfection of the PD-ECGF cDNA into tumour cells may be a novel strategy for gene therapy of cancer, and that it may be possible to increase the therapeutic effects of pyrimidines antimetabolites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

transfection of a PD-ECGF gene into tumour cells may be useful as an approach for cancer therapy, because the transfected tumour cells are more sensitive than parental tumour cells to 5'-deoxy-5-flurouridine (5'DFUR) and 5-fluouracil (FU).
the transfection of PDGF (dThdpase) gene may be useful as gene therapy for cancer treatment.
the transfection of PDGF (dThdpase) cDNA into cancer cell line PC-9 resulted in a 50 fold increase in dThdpase activity and that the transfected cells were highly sensitive to 5-FUR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transfection of PDGF (dThDPase) genes may prove useful as a gene therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment.
the PD-ECGF gene can be transferred into human tumour cells to increase their sensitivity to 5-FUR and 5'-DFU and to induce a bystander effect.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using the PD-ECGF gene for the selective killing of tumour cells by 5'-DFU and tegafur.
